title: HTML Document Lifecycle
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of html document lifecycle in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: This lesson turns “HTML Document Lifecycle” into a practical authoring skill. You will work with document loading and parsing, understand the choices that matter, and check the result instead of relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding browser behavior and boundaries helps you reason about embedded content, interaction, privacy, and how document markup participates in a larger application.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The loading attribute: the requested loading strategy; lazy-load off-screen media, not the primary image needed immediately.

items.title: Document loading and parsing
items.text: The loading attribute: the requested loading strategy; lazy-load off-screen media, not the primary image needed immediately.

items.title: The DOMContentLoaded event
items.text: Browsers parse HTML into a document tree and recover from many authoring errors. Browser recovery is not a substitute for valid markup; inspect the DOM and validate the original source.

items.title: The load event
items.text: The load event is one of the decisions covered by HTML Document Lifecycle. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: Script placement and parsing behavior
items.text: Script placement and parsing behavior is one of the decisions covered by HTML Document Lifecycle. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: The defer attribute
items.text: The defer attribute: runs an external classic script after parsing and preserves document-order execution among deferred scripts.

items.title: The async attribute
items.text: The async attribute: allows a classic external script to run as soon as it is available, so execution order is not guaranteed.

items.title: Module scripts at a conceptual level
items.text: Module scripts at a conceptual level is one of the decisions covered by HTML Document Lifecycle. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: Render-blocking resources at a conceptual level
items.text: Choose resource hints and loading behavior from measurement, not habit. Preserve intrinsic dimensions, avoid lazy-loading content needed immediately, and prioritize only genuinely important resources.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Prefer the native semantic element that communicates intent. Do not choose markup solely for its default visual style.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates html document lifecycle. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from HTML Document Lifecycle.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: HTML Document Lifecycle is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.

Choose resource hints and loading behavior from measurement, not habit. Preserve intrinsic dimensions, avoid lazy-loading content needed immediately, and prioritize only genuinely important resources.
Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
